items.title: Adrian Cunningham interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 31, 2021
items.q: I mean Wycliffe Gordon is one of my biggest influences just in terms of a human being, beyond the music. I’ve been in his quintet for, what, six or seven years now

ctx.x: Are there other things that you learned, like on the bandstand or from older musicians that you had not learned in music school?

Oh yes. I would say ninety percent of it. Ninety percent of what you learn is on the gig you know. From the obvious things, and this is such a cliché, turning up on time, looking good, answering emails or texts when they come in about gigs and not just leaving — you know, all of those obvious things are something that is kind of misplaced I think with young kids coming up, and I was probably like that too as a youngster, a little bit complacent about calling back or being really professional. And I think that’s…

Thanks for saying that. I have this personal feeling about when people think of jazz musicians often times they think they’re playing anything they want. They’re playing how they feel. And it seems that there are certain times when you’re on a gig and you
